subject: Clarifications: identity sync, SSO, and admin controls for Meridian Health RFP
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@meridianhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@meridianhealth.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up questions on your IDAM capability packet

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the packet you uploaded to the RFP portal. We reviewed sections on SSO and provisioning and have a few clarification items before we complete our scoring:  

1) SSO: Do you support both SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect? For SAML please confirm support for both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows and which NameID formats you accept. For OIDC, do you support dynamic client registration and back-channel logout?

2) SCIM provisioning: Does Redwood support SCIM 2.0 with PATCH and bulk operations? How do you handle delta syncs and group membership mappings (nested groups, group-to-role mapping)? Also, what is your typical sync rate limit and error handling for partial failures?

3) RBAC and admin controls: Can you outline your admin role model, whether role definitions are tenant-scoped, and whether customers can create custom roles with least-privilege enforcement? How are delegated admin actions captured in logs?

4) Admin security: Does the console enforce MFA for admin logins, session idle/absolute timeouts, and adaptive authentication? Is there support for just-in-time provisioning when users sign in via SSO?

If you can respond to these in a short email and attach any relevant schemas or mappings, that would be ideal. Our timeline is tight; we need answers by EOD Thursday 2027-09-16.

Best,
Alex Turner
Director, Procurement
Meridian Health
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up questions on your IDAM capability packet

Alex, thanks for the clear set of questions. High level answers are below; attached is a concise PDF with configuration notes and a sample SAML metadata snippet. Ben and Marissa are looped in for deeper SCIM and RBAC details.

1) SSO
- SAML 2.0: Supported (SP-initiated and IdP-initiated). NameID formats supported: persistent, transient, emailAddress. We also support custom NameID mappings by attribute. We publish metadata XML for each tenant and support signed assertions and encryption of assertion and response.
- OIDC: Supported. We support standard OIDC flows including authorization code with PKCE, hybrid, and implicit for legacy clients. Dynamic client registration is available as an opt-in feature for Enterprise tenants via our management API. Back-channel logout is supported; front-channel logout is supported with caveats for older browser flows.

2) SCIM provisioning
- SCIM 2.0 supported with PATCH (RFC 7644). Bulk is supported for initial imports via a separate bulk API endpoint; typical bulk window is intended for onboarding (one-time). Delta sync is implemented via list with startIndex/totalResults and etag-based change detection. Support for groups: we sync Users and Groups; nested groups are flattened during sync but we preserve original group path in a custom attribute if requested. We also provide tenant-level mappings: map group -> application role.
- Rate limits: standard provisioning rate is 60 requests/minute by default for enterprise tenants; can be raised with Dedicated plans. Partial failures: operations are transactional per object where possible; for bulk operations we return per-item status and provide retry guidance.

3) RBAC and admin controls
- Admin model: three built-in tiers (Owner, Admin, Operator) plus fully-customizable role templates. Roles are tenant-scoped by default; customers can create custom roles and scope them to projects or applications. We support role conditions (e.g., read-only for X resource) and permission sets.
- Least privilege: custom role creation enforces UI warnings and a preview of net permissions; programmatic role creation is available via API.
- Delegation: delegated admin actions must be performed by a user with the appropriate role and are logged with actor, action, target, timestamp, and the originating IP. Logs are available in the Console (30 days by default) and can be exported to customer SIEM (via syslog/forwarder) for longer retention.

4) Admin security and provisioning
- MFA: enforced for all admin roles by default; customers can require MFA for all users. Supported methods include TOTP, FIDO2/WebAuthn, and SMS as a fallback (SMS not recommended for admin accounts).
- Sessions: configurable idle and absolute timeouts at tenant-level; default idle timeout 30 minutes, absolute 12 hours.
- Adaptive authentication: supported via risk signals (IP reputation, new device fingerprint).
- Just-in-time provisioning: supported for both SAML and OIDC; you can configure attribute-to-role mapping to create users on first successful SSO.

Attachments in my reply: Meridian_RFP_Response_IDAM_20270914.pdf (detailed configuration notes, SAML metadata snippet, sample SCIM payloads). Ben will follow up with the attribute mapping CSV and a short technical note on error handling and rate limits.

If you want a quick sync, we can set a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the SCIM examples.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Security Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@meridianhealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up questions on your IDAM capability packet

On 2027-09-14 14:30, Irene Choi wrote:
> 1) SSO - SAML 2.0: Supported ...
> 2) SCIM provisioning - SCIM 2.0 supported with PATCH ...

Adding technical detail for SCIM and a sample attribute mapping file attached. Key points:  

- SCIM endpoints: /scim/v2/Users and /scim/v2/Groups. We implement PATCH with operations add, remove, replace. For bulk ingestion we recommend the bulk endpoint (POST /scim/v2/Bulk) for initial imports; the bulk API returns per-item statuses.
- Delta sync: we support ETag and If-None-Match to detect no-change; for change feeds you can use our event webhook for near-real-time updates instead of polling.
- Groups and nested membership: we flatten nested groups on import and create canonical group IDs. If you need nested semantics, we can include a memberOf attribute reflecting the original hierarchy. For mapping group->role we provide a mapping table per tenant (see attached CSV).
- Conflict resolution: authoritative source is customer IdP. When provisioning conflicts occur (e.g., two external sources try to modify an account), we surface a conflict record and provide a manual reconcile workflow in the Console.
- Rate limits and backoff: default 60 req/min; for sustained retries we advise exponential backoff (Retry-After header returned with 429). We log failed operations to the tenant activity log with a correlation ID for support.

Below is a short SAML metadata example you can drop into your IdP. Replace {ENTITY_ID} and {ACS_URL} with your Meridian values:

<md:EntityDescriptor entityID="https://redwood.example/tenants/{ENTITY_ID}">
  <md:SPSSODescriptor AuthnRequestsSigned="true" WantAssertionsSigned="true">
    <md:AssertionConsumerService Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST" Location="{ACS_URL}" index="1"/>
  </md:SPSSODescriptor>
</md:EntityDescriptor>

Attachment: scim-attribute-mapping.csv contains columns: scimPath,scimType,redwoodAttribute,exampleValue,notes. I attached it to this thread and also uploaded to the draft Drive folder.

If Meridian wants our engineers to validate a mapping with a non-prod exchange, we can stand up a temporary provisioning sandbox and run a sample delta sync. Let me know a preferred window.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Product Engineer, Identity
Redwood Inference
